newsitem.title: UK: Scientists in Britain find diabetes genes.
newsitem.headline: Scientists in Britain find diabetes genes.

text.p: Scientists from Oxford University said on Thursday they had helped to track down a network of genes linked to the onset of diabetes in people over 40.
In a statement, the university said the discovery could eventually lead to new ways of tackling the disease.

Work at Oxford and by scientists in the U.S, France, Denmark, Japan and other British institutions, has led to the identification of a group of genes which were not previously thought to play a role in the onset of diabetes.
Diabetes is a common disease caused by lack of control of glucose levels in the blood. Type 1 diabetes tends to affect people under 20 while Type 2 diabetes afflicts older people.

The newly-discovered genes are thought to contribute to the onset of Type 2 diabetes, which affects up to eight percent of people over 60. It is a major cause of blindness, renal faulure, amputations and death.

Roger Cox, who leads the research group at the Oxford-based Diabetes Research Laboratory, said researchers are now working on monitoring changes in the genes of diabetic patients. He said the discovery of the genes "opens up a new avenue of research into the complex genetics of the disease."
